newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Down with Euro", says French eve-of-poll protest.
newsitem.headline: "Down with Euro", says French eve-of-poll protest.

text.p: Several thousand people marched through Paris on Saturday to demand the repeal of the Maastricht Treaty on European unification, in a protest on the eve of France's knife-edge parliamentary vote.
The demonstration was called by the National Committee for the Repeal of the Maastricht Treaty, created by the far-left Workers Party and deputies from the Communist and Citizens Movement parties.
Organisers, who said their anti-Maastricht petition had been signed by 43,000 people, put the number of protesters at between 18,000 and 20,000. Police put the number at 4,200.
Chanting "Down with the single currency", the demonstrators marched from the Bastille square in eastern Paris towards the centre of the city.
Europe has figured prominently in the election campaign. Gaullist President Jacques Chirac called the snap poll saying France needed a "new elan" to help it qualify for the single currency.

Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, tipped as prime minister if the Socialist-Communist bloc wins, has come under fire from the right for laying down conditions on France joining a single currency, which the Communists oppose outright.
Jospin's conditions include relaxing the Maastricht criteria and gearing the single currency towards creating jobs.
